titulo: Module 09 — Claude Code in CI/CD and iterative refinement (review quiz)

questoes.pergunta: Claude generates release notes in an almost-right format, but one that varies between runs. The prose instructions have already been rewritten twice. What is the most effective next step?
opcoes: Rewrite the prose instruction with more emphasis and words in CAPITAL LETTERS
Include 2–3 concrete input → output examples, covering an edge case
Switch to a larger model
Ask it to "use your good judgment to keep the format consistent"
questoes.explicacao: Concrete examples convey format and edge cases better than prose; the model imitates the pattern.
feedbacks: More emphasis on the same prose rarely fixes the variation.
Correct.
A more expensive solution that doesn't attack the cause (format ambiguity).
A vague criterion produces exactly the inconsistency observed.

questoes.pergunta: In the TDD workflow with Claude Code, which rule preserves the value of the tests as the definition of done?
opcoes: Write the tests after the implementation, so they reflect the final code
Let Claude adjust the tests when they seem too rigid
Run the tests only at the end, once
Write the tests first, feed the failures back to Claude, and don't allow it to change the tests to make them pass
questoes.explicacao: The test is the verifiable target; if Claude can change it, the criterion ceases to exist.
feedbacks: Tests written afterward tend to validate what was done, not what was expected.
It opens the door to "passing" by moving the target.
It loses the iteration cycle driven by the failures.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: The PO asked for "a commissions module for salespeople" in two lines, in a domain the team doesn't know. Which technique should you use before writing any code?
opcoes: Ask Claude to interview you with clarifying questions before implementing
Ask for the implementation directly and fix it in review
Use `--max-turns 50` so Claude has room to explore
Send the request via the Batch API to save money
questoes.explicacao: Vague requirement + unfamiliar domain → interview: Claude surfaces rules and edge cases before spending effort on an implementation.
feedbacks: Correct.
It causes rework along the lines of "that's not what I meant".
More turns don't resolve the requirement's ambiguity.
Batch has nothing to do with requirement clarity.

questoes.pergunta: Two bugs in the same `OrderCalculator`: the rounding of the total depends on the order in which discounts are applied, and that order is wrong. How should you send them to Claude?
opcoes: In two separate sessions, one per bug
The rounding one first; the ordering one can wait until another week
In a single message, because the problems interact
Together with all the other 10 open bugs in the backlog
questoes.explicacao: Related problems go together so Claude sees the whole picture; independent ones go in sequence.
feedbacks: Splitting coupled problems makes one fix undo the other.
Fixing one in isolation can be invalidated by the fix for the other.
Correct.
Mixing in independent problems produces an unreviewable diff.

questoes.pergunta: A CI job runs `claude "fix the lint warnings"` and hangs until it times out. What is the cause?
opcoes: `--max-turns` was missing
`-p` was missing: without it, Claude Code opens the interactive session and waits for input
The runner doesn't have access to CLAUDE.md
`--output-format json` was missing
questoes.explicacao: `-p` (or `--print`) is non-interactive mode: it executes, prints, and exits.
feedbacks: It limits turns, but doesn't take the process out of interactive mode.
Correct.
Without CLAUDE.md it would still run; that doesn't explain the hang.
The output format doesn't change interactive mode.

questoes.pergunta: Using `claude -p ... --output-format json --json-schema '<schema>'`, in which field of the output JSON does the schema-conforming response appear?
opcoes: `structured_output`
`result`
`content[0].text`
`session_id`
questoes.explicacao: With `--json-schema`, the validated response comes in `structured_output`; `result` contains the text.
feedbacks: Correct.
`result` is the final text; the schema-conforming object is in `structured_output`.
That's the Messages API format, not the output of `claude -p`.
It's the session identifier.

questoes.pergunta: An internal dashboard needs to show, in real time, each step Claude takes during a CI job. Which output format should you use?
opcoes: `--output-format text`
`--output-format json`
`--json-schema` without `--output-format`
`--output-format stream-json`
questoes.explicacao: `stream-json` emits one JSON object per line as events happen.
feedbacks: Text only at the end, with no structure.
A single object at the end of the run.
The schema defines the format of the final response, not streaming.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: What is the correct role of `--max-turns` in a pipeline?
opcoes: Define when the task is done
Ensure Claude uses exactly N turns
Serve as a backstop that limits cost and time in the worst case
Replace the job's `timeout`
questoes.explicacao: An iteration limit is a backstop; the normal end is Claude finishing. Use it together with the job timeout.
feedbacks: Using an arbitrary limit as the primary stopping mechanism is an anti-pattern.
It's a ceiling, not a target.
Correct.
They're complementary: one limits turns, the other wall-clock time.

questoes.pergunta: In CI, you want to add "You are a senior C# reviewer" while keeping all of Claude Code's default behavior. Which flag?
opcoes: `--system-prompt`
`--append-system-prompt`
`--json-schema`
`--permission-mode plan`
questoes.explicacao: `--append-system-prompt` appends to the default system prompt; `--system-prompt` replaces everything.
feedbacks: It replaces the entire system prompt and loses the default behavior.
Correct.
It defines the output format, not the persona.
It changes the permission posture, not the instructions.

questoes.pergunta: Using `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`, how do you pass `--max-turns 8` and `--allowedTools` to Claude?
opcoes: Through the `claude_args` input
Through the environment variables `MAX_TURNS` and `ALLOWED_TOOLS`
By writing them in the repository's CLAUDE.md
It's not possible; the Action uses fixed values
questoes.explicacao: `claude_args` passes any CLI flag through to Claude Code inside the Action.
feedbacks: Correct.
That's not how the Action receives these options.
CLAUDE.md is for instructions, not flag configuration.
The Action accepts the flags via `claude_args`.

questoes.pergunta: To save money, the team proposes running each PR's mandatory security check through the Batch API. What is your assessment?
opcoes: Good idea: 50% savings with no side effects
Good idea, as long as the batch has more than 100 PRs
Good idea if it uses a `custom_id` equal to the PR number
Bad idea: Batch can take up to 24h with no SLA, incompatible with a blocking pre-merge step
questoes.explicacao: Never use Batch in a blocking/pre-merge step. Use synchronous calls at the gate; use Batch for nightly/weekly analysis.
feedbacks: It ignores latency: the PR would be blocked for hours.
Volume doesn't change the lack of an SLA.
`custom_id` solves correlation, not latency.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: The results of a Batch API batch arrived, and the script assigns each result to a document by its position in the list. Some reports got swapped. What is the fix?
opcoes: Sort the results by creation date
Send one document per batch
Match each result by the `custom_id` defined at submission
Use `--output-format json`
questoes.explicacao: Batch results can come back out of order; `custom_id` is the correlation key.
feedbacks: Order isn't guaranteed by any criterion; don't use position or date.
It throws away the advantage of batching.
Correct.
It's a `claude -p` flag; it has nothing to do with the Batch API.

questoes.pergunta: A job generates code with `claude -p` and, in the next step, runs `claude -p --continue "now review what you wrote"`. The review approves almost everything. What should change?
opcoes: Do the review in a new, independent session, with the diff and explicit criteria
Increase `--max-turns` for the review step
Ask it to "be very critical" in the review prompt
Replace `--continue` with `--resume` using the same ID
questoes.explicacao: The session that generated the code tends to confirm its own decisions (reasoning-context bias). Review in a new session.
feedbacks: Correct.
More turns in the same biased session don't remove the bias.
An instruction doesn't remove the reasoning context that causes the bias.
`--resume` with the same ID is the same session; same problem.

questoes.pergunta: A PR with 45 files gets a superficial review, and cross-module bugs slip through. Which elements make up the recommended approach? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: A single prompt with all 45 files and the instruction "be thorough"
Pass 1: review each file in isolation, with the same criteria
Review only the 10 largest files
Use the Batch API for the PR review
Pass 2: a separate integration prompt that receives the findings from pass 1 and looks for cross-file problems
questoes.explicacao: Multi-pass: local per-file analysis + a cross-file integration pass, with a separate prompt.
feedbacks: That's the cause of the problem: diluted attention and inconsistent criteria.
Correct.
It leaves files unreviewed and doesn't catch cross-file bugs.
PR review is blocking: synchronous.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A CI job only analyzes the code and publishes a report; it must not change anything on the runner. Which settings apply least privilege deterministically? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` to avoid prompts
An instruction in the prompt: "don't modify files"
`--allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob"`
`--permission-mode dontAsk`, denying everything that hasn't been pre-approved
`--allowedTools "Bash"` so Claude can run whatever it needs
questoes.explicacao: Pre-approving only read tools and denying the rest (`dontAsk`) restricts the job deterministically.
feedbacks: It unlocks everything: the opposite of least privilege.
A prompt is probabilistic; it's not a control.
Correct.
Correct.
Unrestricted Bash allows changing anything on the runner.
